title: Letters with two sounds: בּ ב, כּ כ, פּ פ ף
topic: the dagesh: בּ/ב, כּ/כ, פּ/פ; final ף
why: The letter פ, which is read p or f, lets you take stock of the dagesh, the dot that changes the sound of בּ/ב, כּ/כ and פּ/פ. You also learn to ask where something is and to order politely.

{"lessons": ["

New letter: פּ, פ and ף

LetterNameSound
פּpep (with the dot)
פfef (without the dot)
ףfinal fef, at the end of a word

פ looks like כ, with a little tongue hanging inside. Its final form ף goes down below the line, like ך and ן.

פֹּהpo: here
סֵפֶרsefer: book
כֶּסֶףkesef: money

פֹּה (po, here) and פֶּה (pe, mouth): only one vowel tells them apart! פֹּה means the same thing as כָּאן.

", "

The dagesh: a dot that changes the sound

Three letters change their sound depending on the dot (the dagesh):

LetterNameSound
בּbetb
בvetv
כּkafk
כ ךkhaf, final khafkh
פּpep
פ ףfe, final fef

A simple rule of thumb: at the start of a word, these letters almost always have the dot (b, k, p); in the middle or at the end, after a vowel, often not (v, kh, f).

פֶּה — יָפֶהpe: mouth — yafe: beautiful
כֶּלֶב — מֶלֶךְkelev: dog — melekh: king
בַּיִת — תֵּל אָבִיבbayit: house — Tel Aviv

In the other letters (דּ, תּ, גּ, מּ…), the dot doesn't change the sound: אִמָּא is read ima, פִּתָּה is read pita.

", "

Where? Here! Open, closed

אֵיפֹה הַסֵּפֶר? — פֹּה!Where is the book? — Here! [eifo ha-sefer? — po!]
הַמִּסְעָדָה פְּתוּחָה?Is the restaurant open? [ha-mis'ada ptukha?]
לֹא, הִיא סְגוּרָה.No, it's closed. [lo, hi sgura]

A small a under a final ח is read BEFORE the letter: פָּתוּחַ is read pa-tu-akh (open). In the feminine, no more trap: פְּתוּחָה, ptukha.

To order politely, add בְּבַקָּשָׁה (bevakasha, please): קָפֶה, בְּבַקָּשָׁה.

Words borrowed from other languages often keep their sound: טֶלֶפוֹן (telefon), קָפֶה (kafe). The פ without a dot really does make f.
